# Review: housekeeping for the modular vexos-nix justfile

## Files changed

- `catalog/tests/fixtures/vexos-nix-justfile.json`: regenerated by `scripts/refresh-drift-fixture.sh ../vexos-nix/justfile`
- `catalog/src/lib.rs`: module doc updated; the `backup-plex` last-comment-line example is gone
- `catalog/src/drift.rs`: `JustAssignment.value` changed from `String` to `serde_json::Value`, plus a regression case in the unit-test dump

## Finding outside the original spec (fixed)

The refreshed fixture didn't parse:
`invalid type: sequence, expected a string, line 10`. vexos-nix added
`_just := just_executable() + " --justfile " + justfile()`, and `just --dump` writes a
non-literal assignment as a JSON syntax tree, not a string. `JustDump::parse` is
also how the GUI (`src/just.rs`) reads the host's live justfile, so without this fix
any host running the new vexos-nix would show "Could not read this host's justfile" and
lose availability filtering. The fix keeps the raw JSON value. `list_variable` and
`service_catalog` read it with `as_str()`, so an expression reads as "not a literal"
and the whole dump still parses. No catalog actions changed.

## Fixture diff, verified

- Visibility: `service`, `plex-pass`, `zfs-pool`, `mergerfs-pool` changed from private to public
- New private helpers: `pick`, `_pick-target`, `_require-ai`, `_require-nixos`,
  `_require-known-service`, `_confirm-typed`, plus `_remote-storage-list` (not in the brief)
- Parameters of every recipe present before and after: unchanged
- New assignments: `_just` (expression), `_service_runtime`
- Not as the brief said: `_service_catalog` and `_server_service_names` gained 6
  services (chaptarr, listenarr, mediamanager, sportarr, tdarr, wishlist). The format is
  unchanged, and VexPortal reads services from the justfile at runtime, so the
  catalog needs no change.

## Justfile-as-single-file audit

No consumer copies or parses the file. The GUI's dump, its terminal and the daemon's
executor all pass `--justfile /etc/nixos/justfile --working-directory /etc/nixos` to
`just`, and the daemon unit sets `ProtectSystem = false`. No change needed.
